ArtifactCitation.description:
A pointer to evidence that supports an artifact.

Citations are how downstream review can audit a producer's
reasoning : "this MITRE T1078 mapping was supported by event X
section Y at score 0.83". The exact ``source_kind`` vocabulary is
open (``alert``, ``log_event``, ``threat_intel_feed``, etc.) ;
consumers MUST tolerate kinds they don't recognize.
ArtifactCitation.title: ArtifactCitation

ArtifactConfidence.description:
A numeric confidence score paired with a coarse-grained band.

Both fields are optional so that producers without a probabilistic
model can still emit confidence (band only) and probabilistic
producers can emit both. Consumers read whichever is present.
ArtifactConfidence.title: ArtifactConfidence

ArtifactEnvelope.description:
Canonical envelope every read-side artifact rides in.

The ``artifact_type`` string identifies WHAT was produced (an
enrichment, a classification, a MITRE assessment, ...). The
``subject_*`` fields identify what it's ABOUT (an alert or a
case). Producer / confidence / citations carry HOW it was made.
The actual payload of the artifact lives outside the envelope —
typed assessment classes (``ClassificationAssessment``,
``MitreAssessment``, ``EnrichmentAssessment``) compose the
envelope with their specific payload.

This is the read-side analogue of :class:`warlog_spec.provider_abi.AuditRow`
on the write side : a uniform envelope shape that audit, review,
and surface tooling can consume without knowing the producer.
ArtifactEnvelope.title: ArtifactEnvelope

ArtifactProducer.description:
Who or what generated an artifact.

The five kinds map cleanly to the provenance categories that
matter for downstream review : human-authored, rule-based,
ML-model-output, LLM-output, or system-internal (e.g. an
auto-correlator).
ArtifactProducer.title: ArtifactProducer

ArtifactReviewState.description:
Lifecycle state of a produced artifact through human review.

A connector emits artifacts in ``PENDING`` ; analysts move them
through ``ACCEPTED`` / ``REJECTED``. ``SUPERSEDED`` covers the
case where a fresher artifact about the same subject replaces an
older one (e.g. a re-enrichment after the IOC verdict flipped).
ArtifactReviewState.title: ArtifactReviewState

ConfidenceBand.description:
Coarse-grained confidence band used when a numeric score is not the
right surface (e.g. for human-readable summaries or UI badges).
ConfidenceBand.title: ConfidenceBand

MatchedTriggerCondition.description:
One trigger condition, paired with what was actually observed.

``expected`` is configuration and can be re-read from the playbook
at any time ; ``observed`` is evidence and cannot. It is the value
the condition read off THIS signal at trigger time, which is the
part nobody can reconstruct once the signal has moved on — an
alert gets re-scored, re-categorized, closed. Recording only the
configuration would produce an artifact that looks like proof and
proves nothing.

``observed`` is nullable because a condition can be evaluated
against a field the signal does not carry ; ``null`` is then the
honest record of "the field was absent", not a missing value.
MatchedTriggerCondition.title: MatchedTriggerCondition

PlaybookGateEvaluationPayload.description:
Body of a :class:`PlaybookGateEvaluation` artifact.

Under AND semantics a match means every condition held, so
``matched_conditions`` is the full evaluated set rather than a
subset — a reader can therefore treat it as the complete reason.

``conditions_source_hash`` pins the playbook configuration that
was evaluated : it is sha256 of the canonical-bytes serialization
of the trigger-condition list as stored on the playbook. An
auditor comparing it against the playbook's current conditions
can tell whether the rule that fired still exists in that form,
which is the difference between "these conditions matched" and
"these conditions matched and here is the rule that held them".

conditionsSourceHash.description: sha256 of the canonical-bytes serialization of the evaluated trigger conditions
conditionsSourceHash.title: Conditionssourcehash

PlaybookGateEvaluationPayload.title: PlaybookGateEvaluationPayload

description:
Typed record of the deterministic gate that fired an unattended run.

The decision artifact for an action nobody decided. A human click
produces an :class:`ApprovalDecision` and a model proposal
produces a ``*Proposal``; a published playbook whose trigger
conditions matched produces neither, yet
:attr:`~warlog_spec.provider_abi.AuditRow.decision_ref` is
REQUIRED — deliberately, because an action with no traceable
decision is exactly what must not be writable. This artifact is
what that pointer aims at, so the requirement is satisfied by a
real object instead of being relaxed.

Rides inside :class:`ArtifactEnvelope` with
``producer.kind = "rule"`` : the producer was configuration, not a
person and not a model.
title: PlaybookGateEvaluation
